Compare two states over a whole time course

Source: R/compare_timecourse.R
compare_timecourse.Rd

Combines the labeling times of each peptide into whole-time-course statistics, so a peptide is judged on all its time points together rather than one time point at a time.

Usage

compare_timecourse(
  filepath,
  state1,
  state2,
  times,
  alpha = 0.01,
  pvalue = 0.01,
  p_adjust = "none",
  min_timepoints = 2,
  percent = FALSE,
  replicates = NULL
)

Arguments

filepath

input file or table, as for output_tp().

state1, state2

the two protein states (differences are state2 - state1).

times

time points to combine. Default: all common time points.

alpha

alpha of the critical intervals. Default 0.01.

pvalue

p-value cutoff. Default 0.01.

p_adjust

multiple-testing correction passed to stats::p.adjust(): "none" (default) or e.g. "BH"; across peptides for the summed test, and across peptides within each time for the per-time calls.

min_timepoints

number of time points at which a peptide must pass the per-time rule for sig_min_timepoints. Default 2.

percent

value scale as in output_tp(): FALSE (Da, default), TRUE, "FD" or "per_residue".

replicates

optional maximum number of replicates per state.

Value

data frame with one row per peptide: Start, End, Sequence, Charge, n_times, summed_delta, se, df, p_value, p_adj, ci_sum, sig_summed, n_timepoints_sig, sig_min_timepoints, and one sig_<time> column per time point.

Details

For each peptide (present at every requested time in both states):

Summed difference

summed_delta = sum over time points of (mean state2 - mean state1), in Da (or percent). Its standard error combines the per-time standard errors, p_value is a Welch-type t-test of the sum (Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom), and ci_sum is a global critical interval for summed differences: the per-time pooled Hageman & Weis standard errors combined over time points, times |qt(alpha/2, df)|. sig_summed uses the package-wide rule: (adjusted) p < pvalue AND |summed_delta| > ci_sum.

Per time point

the usual peptide rule at each time (Welch p, adjusted across peptides within that time with p_adjust, below pvalue AND |delta| > that time's pooled CI); n_timepoints_sig is how many time points pass, and sig_min_timepoints whether that is at least min_timepoints.

See also

robot_indexes(), woods_CI_plot(), compare_regions()

Examples

file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
tc <- compare_timecourse(file_nm, "Unbound", "bound")
head(tc[order(tc$p_value), ])
